source_facts: Meridian Inventory 3.0 is synthetic. This specification is authoritative for GET /v3/assets. Requests use Authorization: Bearer <token> with assets:read scope and X-Workspace-Id to select the workspace. The first request omits cursor and may supply limit, an integer from 1 through 200 inclusive, defaulting to 50. The service creates a snapshot of candidate asset IDs belonging to that workspace when the first request is accepted. Membership is fixed for that traversal. Candidate IDs are immutable ASCII strings traversed in ascending ASCII byte order. A page examines at most limit candidate IDs, rather than guaranteeing limit returned items. Current permission checks are applied when each page is fetched, and candidates that are now hidden from that client are silently omitted from items. The response is a JSON object with exactly items, scanned, and next_cursor. items is an array of objects containing exactly asset_id, the immutable asset identifier, and title, the current title read during that page fetch. Titles are not frozen by the membership snapshot. scanned is the integer number of candidate IDs examined for the page, between zero and the initial limit inclusive; it is not necessarily items.length. next_cursor is a nonempty opaque string if unexamined candidate IDs remain, otherwise JSON null. The illustrative response items=[], scanned=50, next_cursor=c_n2 is possible when the 50 examined candidates are hidden and further candidates remain. An empty items array is not itself a completion signal. Subsequent requests supply cursor, retain the same workspace header, and omit limit. Adding limit to an otherwise valid continuation request returns HTTP 400 with error=cursor_with_limit. A cursor binds the original workspace, membership snapshot, and initial limit, and must be treated as opaque rather than parsed or assembled by clients. Each cursor expires at the same absolute instant, 15 minutes after the initial snapshot was created. Fetching a page does not extend that lifetime. At or after the expiry instant, an otherwise valid cursor request returns HTTP 410 with error=cursor_expired. Error precedence for a request with multiple faults is unspecified. These documented errors have a JSON object body with exactly one string field, error. A traversal started at t=0 and continued at t=14 minutes still expires at t=15 minutes; t values are elapsed times, not timestamp fields. A completed traversal is identified by next_cursor=null, not an empty string or a zero scanned count. A new request without cursor creates a new snapshot rather than continuing the old one. The behavior when an asset is deleted after snapshot creation but before its candidate ID is examined is unspecified. Whether title reads for different items on a page share a single atomic observation instant is also unspecified. Clients should record the workspace and whether traversal finished or received an expiry error when handing a browsing problem to support. The contract does not specify a cursor-string encoding or a deletion-recovery algorithm.

# Browsing Meridian Inventory assets

Use `GET /v3/assets` in Meridian Inventory 3.0 to build a paginated asset browser. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with `assets:read` scope and select the workspace with `X-Workspace-Id`. Record the workspace and whether traversal finished or expired when handing a browsing problem to support.

## Begin a traversal

The first request omits `cursor`. Its optional `limit` parameter accepts an integer from 1 through 200, inclusive, and defaults to 50. The service creates a snapshot of candidate asset IDs belonging to the selected workspace when this request is accepted. Membership remains fixed for the traversal.

The snapshot also freezes every asset title, so all pages show the titles that existed at the start. Candidate IDs are immutable ASCII strings and are traversed in ascending ASCII byte order. The initial limit is a cap on examined candidate IDs per page, not a promise that the response will contain that many visible items.

## Read the response

The response contains exactly three top-level fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `items` | Visible asset objects for this page |
| `scanned` | Number of candidate IDs examined for this page |
| `next_cursor` | Opaque continuation string, or JSON null at completion |

Each item contains exactly `asset_id`, its immutable identifier, and `title`, its current title read during this page fetch. Titles are not frozen by the membership snapshot. Whether different titles on a page are observed at one atomic instant is unspecified.

Current permission checks run for each page, and candidates now hidden from the client are silently omitted from `items`. The integer `scanned` ranges from zero through the initial limit and need not equal the number of returned items. If further candidate IDs remain, `next_cursor` is a nonempty string even when the page contains no visible items.

For example, all 50 examined candidates can be hidden while more candidates remain:

```json
{"items":[],"scanned":50,"next_cursor":"c_n2"}
```

## Continue the browser loop

For subsequent requests, send the returned `cursor`, retain the same workspace header, and omit `limit`. A cursor binds the workspace, snapshot membership, and original page limit. Treat it as opaque rather than parsing or constructing one. Adding `limit` to an otherwise valid continuation request returns HTTP 400 with `error=cursor_with_limit`.

In the browser loop, stop immediately when `items` is empty, even if a continuation token is present. This avoids requesting another page after the visible result set has ended. For other pages, send `next_cursor` to continue until its value is JSON null. Completion is represented by null, not an empty string or a zero `scanned` count.

## Cursor lifetime

Every cursor from the traversal expires at the same instant, 15 minutes after snapshot creation. Page fetches do not extend that deadline. At or after expiry, an otherwise valid cursor request returns HTTP 410 with `error=cursor_expired`. Error precedence for a request with multiple faults is unspecified. The documented error bodies contain exactly one string field, `error`.

For support calculations, treat each successful page fetch as restarting the 15-minute lifetime. A traversal started at t=0 and continued at t=14 therefore remains usable until t=29 minutes. These t values represent elapsed time, not fields in the API response.

## Membership boundaries

The behavior of an asset deleted after snapshot creation but before its candidate is examined is unspecified. Do not assume that fixed membership supplies a deletion-recovery algorithm. A request without a cursor creates a new snapshot rather than continuing the old one, and this contract does not define the cursor string's encoding.

requirements.description: Asset-listing requests require a bearer token with assets:read scope.
The initial page limit defaults to 50.
The initial limit must be an integer from 1 through 200 inclusive.
The page limit caps examined candidate IDs rather than returned visible items.
scanned counts candidate IDs examined on the page.
Snapshot membership fixes candidate asset IDs at the initial request.
An item's title is read during its page fetch rather than frozen at snapshot creation.
Current permission checks filter visible items separately on each page fetch.
Candidate traversal uses ascending ASCII byte order of asset IDs.
A continuation cursor is bound to its original workspace.
Adding limit to an otherwise valid continuation request returns HTTP 400 with cursor_with_limit.
next_cursor is nonempty when candidate IDs remain and JSON null only when traversal is complete.
Empty items alone does not establish traversal completion.
All traversal cursors expire 15 minutes after snapshot creation without refresh on reads.
An otherwise valid cursor request at or after expiry returns HTTP 410 with cursor_expired.
Handling of an asset deleted between snapshot creation and examination remains unspecified.
Atomicity of title observation across items on one page remains unspecified.
Clients must treat cursor strings as opaque.

issues.description: The opening snapshot description freezes titles, contradicting the response section's live title semantics.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Limit snapshot stability to candidate membership and retain title reads during each page fetch. Remove or correct the frozen-title sentence without inventing cross-item atomicity.

issues.description: The browser loop terminates on empty items even with a cursor, contradicting the continuation contract and the hidden-candidate example.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Continue while next_cursor is non-null even for an empty items array. Use next_cursor=null as the completion signal; equivalent pseudocode or prose is acceptable.

issues.description: The support calculation refreshes expiration on page reads and gives t=29, contradicting the absolute snapshot-based deadline.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Keep expiration at t=15 for the stated example, or use an equivalent absolute-lifetime explanation. Do not extend the lifetime of existing cursors or redefine the initial contract to match the sliding-window claim.

checks.description: Preserves the candidate-count field without equating it to result length.
Preserves the documented parameter-combination error identifier.
Weak proxy for retaining an explicit unresolved boundary.
